targetName: Star Axis Aperture and Solar Pyramid

objectClass.notes: A truncated, tapered stone observatory pylon with a full-height triangular entry, an upper rectangular sight box, a protruding circular metal oculus, paired summit rods, and a repeated edge stair. The close-up aperture photo is admitted only as proportion/material evidence because it lacks an isolable object silhouette.

reasoning: The outer silhouette is a truncated pylon rather than a pointed pyramid.
Identity depends on the relationship among the triangular entry, upper rectangular opening, and protruding circular oculus.
Irregular stone courses and the repeated edge stair create high meso/micro detail density without requiring a high polygon body.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: The north and rear faces are not visible; infer a compatible tapered shell while preserving the previously requested through-passage.
Exact dimensions are unavailable; proportions are matched to the supplied photograph and existing 55-foot site scale.
The close-up oculus photograph establishes shallow-bore framing but does not prove the tube's exterior attachment depth.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Flat, narrow summit cap replaces a pointed apex.
Two slim alignment rods project above the cap.
Deep rectangular opening below the summit.
Circular metal tube protrudes from the lower half of the sight box.
Tall triangular entry reaches from grade to roughly mid-height.
Irregular polygonal and rectangular granite slab joints cover the front face.
Repeated stair treads climb the left sloping edge.
West face reads cool and substantially darker than the sunlit front.
Stone seams carry dark cavity response and remain legible in grazing light.
Subtle vertical weathering and warm/cool slab variation break uniformity.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The exterior reads as the photographed truncated observatory pylon, not a pointed generic pyramid.
The south face includes the full-height narrow triangular entrance, the deep upper rectangular sight box, and a protruding circular metal oculus in the photographed proportions.
The close-up upper-room view has a shallow, broad ring whose clear sky opening occupies at least 72% of the visible outer diameter.
Irregular granite slab courses, cool shadow-side variation, paired summit rods, and the left edge stair remain legible without dropping the validated 60 FPS target.
The existing walk-through Hour Chamber remains open from south to north despite the unseen rear face being inferred.

featureGroups.name: Truncated pylon silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Broad base, steep taper, flat narrow cap, and asymmetric three-quarter depth match the exterior photograph.
failureModes: cap is too wide or body taper is too shallow

featureGroups.name: Upper rectangular sight box and circular oculus
qualityCriteria: A deep rectangular upper opening contains a separately modeled protruding circular tube and dark reveal.
The close-up aperture uses a shallow bore with a sky-to-outer-diameter ratio of at least 0.72.
failureModes: upper opening is missing or rendered as a flat dark patch
tube is so deep that the clear sky opening reads as a small dot

featureGroups.name: Triangular Hour Chamber entry and through-passage
qualityCriteria: The south opening rises from grade as a narrow triangle and connects continuously to the north opening with complete floor, walls, and ceiling.
failureModes: entry becomes a short floating slit
interior walls disappear or the far opening is sealed

featureGroups.name: Irregular granite slab cladding
qualityCriteria: Front and side faces use irregular nonuniform slab joints rather than a uniform checker grid.
Seams are cavity-darkened and slab values vary subtly across macro, meso, and micro scales.
Independent albedo, roughness, normal, and AO evidence is retained from the admitted stone crop.
failureModes: surface reads as a flat procedural checkerboard
all slabs have identical size, value, and seam spacing

featureGroups.name: Left edge stair, summit cap, and rods
qualityCriteria: A repeated tread system climbs the photographed left sloping edge.
The flat summit carries two thin, separately attached rods.
All repeated parts are stable child nodes or instanced systems.
failureModes: edge stair is absent or placed on the wrong silhouette
summit resolves to a point or lacks the paired rods

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
